topic.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Equations and Inequalities
topic.summary: Solving exponential and logarithmic equations and inequalities with properties and inverses, checking for extraneous solutions, rewriting exponential expressions with logarithms, and finding inverses of transformed exponential and logarithmic functions.

lesson.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Equations and Inequalities
lesson.summary: Solving exponential and logarithmic equations and inequalities with properties and inverses, checking for extraneous solutions, rewriting exponential expressions with logarithms, and finding inverses of transformed exponential and logarithmic functions.
learningGoals: 2.13.A Solve exponential and logarithmic equations and inequalities.
2.13.B Construct the inverse function for exponential and logarithmic functions.
lesson.bigIdea: To solve for a variable in an exponent, take a logarithm; to solve for a variable inside a logarithm, exponentiate. Then check each answer, because the domain of a logarithm can rule some out.
lesson.context: Free-response Question 4 on the AP Exam asks you to solve exponential and logarithmic equations without a calculator and to show every step. This topic brings together the properties from Topics 2.4 and 2.12.

sections.title: 2.13.A · Use properties and the inverse relationship to solve equations and inequalities.

blocks.text: Properties of exponents, properties of logarithms, and the inverse relationship between exponential and logarithmic functions can be used to solve equations and inequalities involving exponents and logarithms.

Inequalities follow the same steps, as long as the function applied to both sides preserves the order. Because 2ˣ is always increasing, 2ˣ > 32 = 2⁵ gives x > 5. Because (1/2)ˣ is always decreasing, (1/2)ˣ > 1/32 gives x < 5.

blocks.title: Write it like the AP Exam

sections.takeaway: Exponent unknown: take a log. Log unknown: exponentiate. Decreasing functions reverse inequalities.

sections.title: 2.13.A · Check solutions for extraneous solutions.

blocks.text: When solving exponential and logarithmic equations found through analytical or graphical methods, the results should be examined for extraneous solutions precluded by the mathematical or contextual limitations.

Example: log₂ x + log₂ (x − 2) = 3. The product property gives log₂ (x(x − 2)) = 3, so x² − 2x = 8 and (x − 4)(x + 2) = 0. The value x = −2 is extraneous, because log₂ (−2) is undefined. The only solution is x = 4.

blocks.title: Write it like the AP Exam
blocks.text: x = −2 is not a solution because −2 is not in the domain of log₂ x. Therefore x = 4.

sections.takeaway: Every argument of every logarithm must be positive at the solution.

sections.title: 2.13.A · Logarithms can rewrite exponential expressions.

blocks.text: Logarithms can be used to rewrite expressions involving exponential functions in different ways that may reveal helpful information. Specifically, bˣ = c^((log_c b)(x)).
Example: 2ˣ = e^((ln 2)x) ≈ e^(0.693x). A model written with base e shows a continuous rate, while the same model written with base 2 shows a doubling.

sections.takeaway: Any exponential can be rewritten with any other base: bˣ = c^((log_c b)x).

sections.title: 2.13.B · Find inverses of transformed exponential and logarithmic functions.

blocks.text: The function f(x) = ab^(x + h) + k is a combination of additive transformations of an exponential function in general form. The inverse of y = f(x) can be found by determining the inverse operations to reverse the mapping.

The function f(x) = a log_b (x + h) + k is a combination of additive transformations of a logarithmic function in general form. The inverse of y = f(x) can be found by determining the inverse operations to reverse the mapping.

blocks.title: Write it like the AP Exam

sections.takeaway: Undo k, then a, then the exponential or logarithm, then h.

vocabulary.definition: When solving exponential and logarithmic equations found through analytical or graphical methods, the results should be examined for extraneous solutions precluded by the mathematical or contextual limitations.

connections.title: Inverse operations
connections.body: Topic 2.8 found inverses by reversing the roles of x and y. Topic 2.10 showed that log_b x undoes bˣ. Both ideas are used here to solve equations and build inverses.

connections.title: Logarithmic models
connections.body: Topic 2.14 builds logarithmic models from data and context, and solving equations like these answers questions about those models.
